@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=6345 sha256=ae0903a9920e71542604329cafce1ece9a47827b8f5fde19508b28dda178d10d path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/BicyclicInterface.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.CycleRank

/-!
# The branching kernel interface — deliberately `OPEN`

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Forest components (excess `0`) and isolated cycle components (excess `1`) of the contact graph
are eliminated exactly in `Anchored/ForestElimination.lean` and
`Anchored/CycleElimination.lean`.  What remains after peeling is a finite **leafless**
instance — a *branching kernel* — whose satisfiability is still exactly decidable, but whose
*global rejection* is **not** proved here and is not proved anywhere in this repository.

This file
* states the global rejection statement `BranchingKernelRejection` as a *parameterised
  interface* which is deliberately **not inhabited** (the `OPEN` node of this route);
* proves the hostile firewall `branchingKernelRejection_unconditional_false`: without a
  hypothesis restricting the kernels to those actually produced by the projection, the
  statement is plainly false — an explicit satisfiable leafless instance of excess `2` is
  exhibited;
* records the endpoint theorem of the route (`anchored_contact_endpoint`).
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

open ContactCSP

/-- **The `OPEN` global step.**  `Arises` is the (here unformalised) predicate selecting the
contact instances actually produced by the high-power projection.  Rejection of *all* the
resulting branching kernels is the open node of this route; no inhabitant is provided. -/
def BranchingKernelRejection (Arises : ContactCSP → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ I : ContactCSP, Arises I → Leafless I → 2 ≤ I.excess → ¬ I.Sat

/-- An explicit satisfiable leafless contact instance of excess `2`. -/
def bicyclicWitness : ContactCSP :=
  { V := {0, 1}
    dom := fun _ _ => true
    Edges := {(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, 0)}
    rel := fun _ _ _ _ => true }

theorem bicyclicWitness_sat : bicyclicWitness.Sat :=
  ⟨fun _ => false, by intro v _; rfl, by intro e _; rfl⟩

theorem bicyclicWitness_excess : bicyclicWitness.excess = 2 := by
  have hV : bicyclicWitness.V.card = 2 := by decide
  have hE : bicyclicWitness.Edges.card = 3 := by decide
  simp only [excess, hV, hE]
  norm_num

theorem bicyclicWitness_leafless : Leafless bicyclicWitness := by
  rintro ⟨x, y, -, -, hxy, hedge, hiso⟩
  have hmem : (x, y) = ((0 : ℕ), (1 : ℕ)) ∨ (x, y) = ((1 : ℕ), (0 : ℕ)) ∨
      (x, y) = ((0 : ℕ), (0 : ℕ)) := by
    simpa [bicyclicWitness, Finset.mem_insert] using hedge
  rcases hmem with h | h | h
  · have hx : x = 0 := congrArg Prod.fst h
    have h10 : ((1 : ℕ), (0 : ℕ)) ∈ bicyclicWitness.Edges := by decide
    have hne : ((1 : ℕ), (0 : ℕ)) ≠ (x, y) := by
      intro hcon
      exact absurd (congrArg Prod.fst hcon) (by omega)
    have := (hiso _ h10 hne).2
    simp [hx] at this
  · have hx : x = 1 := congrArg Prod.fst h
    have h01 : ((0 : ℕ), (1 : ℕ)) ∈ bicyclicWitness.Edges := by decide
    have hne : ((0 : ℕ), (1 : ℕ)) ≠ (x, y) := by
      intro hcon
      exact absurd (congrArg Prod.fst hcon) (by omega)
    have := (hiso _ h01 hne).2
    simp [hx] at this
  · exact hxy ((congrArg Prod.fst h).trans (congrArg Prod.snd h).symm)

/-- **`branchingKernelRejection_unconditional_false`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` hostile firewall.
The global rejection is false without a hypothesis restricting attention to the kernels the
projection actually produces: `bicyclicWitness` is leafless, of excess `2`, and satisfiable. -/
theorem branchingKernelRejection_unconditional_false :
    ¬ BranchingKernelRejection (fun _ => True) := by
  intro h
  exact h bicyclicWitness trivial bicyclicWitness_leafless
    (by rw [bicyclicWitness_excess]) bicyclicWitness_sat

/-! ## A.21  The endpoint theorem of the anchored route -/

/-- **`anchored_contact_endpoint`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For every finite contact instance:

1. satisfiability is exactly decided by the finite procedure `satB`;
2. a forest component (one peeling to an edgeless instance) is decided exactly by
   nonemptiness of the surviving unary domains;
3. an isolated cycle component is decided exactly by the four-pair transfer criterion;
4. every remaining component reduces, by exact leaf eliminations, to a finite leafless
   branching kernel, with satisfiability preserved and still exactly decidable.

The *global rejection* of the branching kernels is **not** part of this theorem; it is the
`OPEN` node `BranchingKernelRejection`. -/
theorem anchored_contact_endpoint (I : ContactCSP) (hwf : I.WellFormed) :
    (I.Sat ↔ I.satB = true) ∧
    (∀ J, Peel I J → J.Edges = ∅ → (I.Sat ↔ ∀ v ∈ J.V, ∃ b : Bool, J.dom v b = true)) ∧
    (∀ (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool) (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ),
      (x :: l).Nodup → I = cycleCSP dom rel x l →
        (I.Sat ↔ ∃ a b : Bool,
          transfer dom rel x l a b = true ∧ rel (lastOf x l) x b a = true)) ∧
    (∃ J, Peel I J ∧ Leafless J ∧ (I.Sat ↔ J.Sat) ∧
      (J.WellFormed → (J.Sat ↔ J.satB = true))) := by
  refine ⟨I.sat_iff_satB hwf, ?_, ?_, peel_to_leafless_decidable I⟩
  · intro J hJ hJE
    exact forest_decision hJ hJE
  · rintro dom rel x l hnd rfl
    exact cycleCSP_sat_iff dom rel x l hnd

/-- **`anchored_endpoint_of_layerRel`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The same endpoint for an instance
whose contact relations are *realized* by the anchored prime-power layer relations: the edge
relations are then exactly the local contact relations of the layers, and all four clauses of
`anchored_contact_endpoint` apply verbatim. -/
theorem anchored_endpoint_of_layerRel (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (Cof : ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (I : ContactCSP) (hwf : I.WellFormed)
    (hreal : ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, ∀ a b : Bool,
      I.rel e.1 e.2 a b = layerRel p (Cof e.1) e.1 a b) :
    (∀ e ∈ I.Edges, ∀ a b : Bool,
        (I.rel e.1 e.2 a b = true ↔ LayerAllows p (Cof e.1) (Cof e.1) (sigPair e.1 a b))) ∧
    (I.Sat ↔ I.satB = true) ∧
    (∃ J, Peel I J ∧ Leafless J ∧ (I.Sat ↔ J.Sat) ∧
      (J.WellFormed → (J.Sat ↔ J.satB = true))) := by
  refine ⟨?_, I.sat_iff_satB hwf, peel_to_leafless_decidable I⟩
  intro e he a b
  rw [hreal e he a b]
  exact layerRel_spec p (Cof e.1) e.1 a b

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8161 sha256=4fc3ced106dce4490c07d84635d943202e0338eb749aff06cb1dfeb68564f7a8 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/ContactGraph.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.PrimePowerLayer

/-!
# Local contact relations and the finite contact graph

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Each arithmetic layer exposes a finite set of *contact positions* `J ⊆ C`.  Its allowed
Boolean signatures

`R_p ⊆ {0,1}^J`

are obtained by existentially quantifying all noncontact cofactors and requiring the **full**
anchored prime-power equation — not a leading-digit surrogate.  This file proves

* `layerAllows_iff`: the signature relation is exactly "there is a subset of `C` agreeing
  with the signature on the contact positions and satisfying the full local condition";
* `layerRel_spec`: the Boolean two-contact relation is exact and *computable*, through the
  fingerprint criterion;

and sets up the finite contact-graph constraint system (`ContactCSP`) with its exact decision
procedure `satB` (`sat_iff_satB`).  Everything is finite; no asymptotic notion occurs.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-! ## A.11  Signatures on the contact positions -/

/-- The contact positions selected by the signature `σ`. -/
def selNodes (contact : Finset ℕ) (σ : ℕ → Bool) : Finset ℕ :=
  contact.filter (fun c => σ c = true)

/-- The contact positions omitted by the signature `σ`. -/
def omitNodes (contact : Finset ℕ) (σ : ℕ → Bool) : Finset ℕ :=
  contact.filter (fun c => σ c = false)

theorem anchor_of_signature {C contact : Finset ℕ} (hsub : contact ⊆ C) (σ : ℕ → Bool) :
    Anchor C (selNodes contact σ) (omitNodes contact σ) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact (Finset.filter_subset _ _).trans hsub
  · exact (Finset.filter_subset _ _).trans hsub
  · refine Finset.disjoint_left.2 ?_
    intro a ha ha'
    simp only [selNodes, omitNodes, Finset.mem_filter] at ha ha'
    exact absurd (ha.2.symm.trans ha'.2) (by simp)

/-- **The local contact relation.**  A signature `σ` on the contact positions of the layer
`(p, C, contact)` is allowed when the anchored state it pins down is locally feasible. -/
def LayerAllows (p : ℕ) (C contact : Finset ℕ) (σ : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  AnchoredFeasible p C (selNodes contact σ) (omitNodes contact σ)

/-- **`layerAllows_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The contact relation is exactly the existential
quantification over the noncontact cofactors of the full local prime-power condition. -/
theorem layerAllows_iff (p : ℕ) {C contact : Finset ℕ} (σ : ℕ → Bool) :
    LayerAllows p C contact σ ↔
      ∃ E, E ⊆ C ∧ (∀ c ∈ contact, (c ∈ E ↔ σ c = true)) ∧
        (recipSum E = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum E)) := by
  unfold LayerAllows AnchoredFeasible
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    rw [mem_allowed] at hE
    refine ⟨E, hE.2.1, ?_, h⟩
    intro c hc
    constructor
    · intro hcE
      by_contra hσ
      have hcN : c ∈ omitNodes contact σ := by
        simp only [omitNodes, Finset.mem_filter]
        exact ⟨hc, by simpa using hσ⟩
      exact (Finset.disjoint_left.1 hE.2.2 hcE) hcN
    · intro hσ
      exact hE.1 (by simp only [selNodes, Finset.mem_filter]; exact ⟨hc, hσ⟩)
  · rintro ⟨E, hEC, hagree, h⟩
    refine ⟨E, mem_allowed.2 ⟨?_, hEC, ?_⟩, h⟩
    · intro c hc
      simp only [selNodes, Finset.mem_filter] at hc
      exact (hagree c hc.1).2 hc.2
    · refine Finset.disjoint_left.2 ?_
      intro c hcE hcN
      simp only [omitNodes, Finset.mem_filter] at hcN
      have := (hagree c hcN.1).1 hcE
      simp [hcN.2] at this

/-! ## A.12  The computable two-contact relation -/

/-- The signature with value `a` at `x` and `b` elsewhere. -/
def sigPair (x : ℕ) (a b : Bool) : ℕ → Bool := fun z => if z = x then a else b

@[simp] theorem sigPair_left (x : ℕ) (a b : Bool) : sigPair x a b x = a := by simp [sigPair]

theorem sigPair_right {x y : ℕ} (h : y ≠ x) (a b : Bool) : sigPair x a b y = b := by
  simp [sigPair, h]

/-- The **Boolean** two-contact relation of a layer, computable through the fingerprint
criterion. -/
def layerRel (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C : Finset ℕ) (x : ℕ) (a b : Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (AnchoredFeasible p C (selNodes C (sigPair x a b)) (omitNodes C (sigPair x a b)))

/-- **`layerRel_spec`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The Boolean relation decides the contact relation
exactly. -/
theorem layerRel_spec (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C : Finset ℕ) (x : ℕ) (a b : Bool) :
    layerRel p C x a b = true ↔ LayerAllows p C C (sigPair x a b) := by
  simp [layerRel, LayerAllows]

/-! ## A.13  The finite contact-graph constraint system -/

/-- A finite binary constraint system on contact positions: vertices `V`, unary domains
`dom`, contact edges `Edges` and a Boolean binary relation `rel` for each edge. -/
structure ContactCSP where
  /-- the contact positions -/
  V : Finset ℕ
  /-- the unary domain indicator at each position -/
  dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool
  /-- the contact edges -/
  Edges : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)
  /-- the binary relation carried by each edge -/
  rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool

namespace ContactCSP

/-- A global Boolean assignment satisfies the instance. -/
def Sat (I : ContactCSP) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → Bool, (∀ v ∈ I.V, I.dom v (f v) = true) ∧
    ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, I.rel e.1 e.2 (f e.1) (f e.2) = true

/-- Endpoints of every edge are positions of the instance. -/
def WellFormed (I : ContactCSP) : Prop := ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, e.1 ∈ I.V ∧ e.2 ∈ I.V

/-- The exact finite search over the powerset of `V`. -/
def SatSearch (I : ContactCSP) : Prop :=
  ∃ S ∈ I.V.powerset, (∀ v ∈ I.V, I.dom v (decide (v ∈ S)) = true) ∧
    (∀ e ∈ I.Edges, I.rel e.1 e.2 (decide (e.1 ∈ S)) (decide (e.2 ∈ S)) = true)

instance decidableSatSearch (I : ContactCSP) : Decidable I.SatSearch := by
  unfold ContactCSP.SatSearch
  infer_instance

/-- The exact finite decision procedure. -/
def satB (I : ContactCSP) : Bool := decide I.SatSearch

/-- **`sat_iff_satSearch`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Satisfiability of a finite contact instance
is exactly the finite powerset search. -/
theorem sat_iff_satSearch (I : ContactCSP) (hwf : I.WellFormed) : I.Sat ↔ I.SatSearch := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hdom, hrel⟩
    refine ⟨I.V.filter (fun v => f v = true), Finset.mem_powerset.2 (Finset.filter_subset _ _),
      ?_, ?_⟩
    · have hval : ∀ v ∈ I.V, (decide (v ∈ I.V.filter (fun w => f w = true))) = f v := by
        intro v hv
        by_cases hfv : f v = true <;> simp [Finset.mem_filter, hv, hfv]
      intro v hv
      rw [hval v hv]
      exact hdom v hv
    · have hval : ∀ v ∈ I.V, (decide (v ∈ I.V.filter (fun w => f w = true))) = f v := by
        intro v hv
        by_cases hfv : f v = true <;> simp [Finset.mem_filter, hv, hfv]
      intro e he
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hwf e he
      rw [hval e.1 h1, hval e.2 h2]
      exact hrel e he
  · rintro ⟨S, -, hd, hr⟩
    exact ⟨fun v => decide (v ∈ S), hd, hr⟩

/-- **`sat_iff_satB`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The Boolean procedure `satB` decides
satisfiability exactly. -/
theorem sat_iff_satB (I : ContactCSP) (hwf : I.WellFormed) : I.Sat ↔ I.satB = true := by
  rw [sat_iff_satSearch I hwf, satB, decide_eq_true_iff]

/-- Consequently satisfiability of a well-formed finite contact instance is decidable. -/
def decidableSat (I : ContactCSP) (hwf : I.WellFormed) : Decidable I.Sat :=
  decidable_of_iff _ (I.sat_iff_satSearch hwf).symm

/-- With no contact edges, satisfiability is exactly nonemptiness of every unary domain. -/
theorem sat_iff_domains_nonempty_of_no_edges (I : ContactCSP) (hE : I.Edges = ∅) :
    I.Sat ↔ ∀ v ∈ I.V, ∃ b : Bool, I.dom v b = true := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hdom, -⟩ v hv
    exact ⟨f v, hdom v hv⟩
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun v => if hv : ∃ b : Bool, I.dom v b = true then hv.choose else false, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      have hex := h v hv
      simp only [dif_pos hex]
      exact hex.choose_spec
    · intro e he
      rw [hE] at he
      exact absurd he (by simp)

end ContactCSP

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5283 sha256=4c6442db986b1c332069d5e39621a0c7aeafc5fdabcb493a7e8826552b88fe47 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/Core.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.Core

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Anchored / contact-graph route, core conventions

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This namespace (`Erdos287.Anchored`) is a *new, append-only, proof-side* development.  It is
deliberately kept disjoint from

* **Route S** — the Source / FivePrime / Directed-Selberg / physical-`k = 1` programme, and
* **Route D** — the Direct Reciprocal programme of `Erdos287.Direct`,

and it must not be conflated with either.  No node of this route discharges a node of another
route unless an explicit bridge theorem is proved; see `Anchored/Reconciliation.lean`.

This file fixes the exact finite conventions of the anchored route:

* the reciprocal sum of a finite set of cofactors (reusing `Erdos287.Direct.recipSum`, so
  that the two routes speak about literally the same rational number);
* the ambient lcm `lcmOf C` of a finite cofactor set, its positivity and divisibility;
* the *integral* cofactor numerator `cofactorNum C E = ∑_{c ∈ E} lcmOf C / c`;
* the exact identity `recipSum E = cofactorNum C E / lcmOf C`.

Everything is finite and exact: sums are rational, no real number and no asymptotic notion
occurs anywhere in this namespace.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-- The reciprocal sum of a finite set of cofactors.  This is *literally* the Route-D
reciprocal sum, reused so that no second convention is introduced. -/
abbrev recipSum (A : Finset ℕ) : ℚ := Erdos287.Direct.recipSum A

theorem recipSum_def (A : Finset ℕ) : recipSum A = ∑ n ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / n := rfl

@[simp] theorem recipSum_empty : recipSum ∅ = 0 := Erdos287.Direct.recipSum_empty

/-- Reciprocal sums are never negative (the convention `1 / (0 : ℚ) = 0` is harmless here). -/
theorem recipSum_nonneg (A : Finset ℕ) : 0 ≤ recipSum A := by
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg ?_
  intro n _
  positivity

/-- On a set of positive cofactors a nonempty subset has a strictly positive reciprocal sum. -/
theorem recipSum_pos {A : Finset ℕ} (hne : A.Nonempty) (hpos : ∀ c ∈ A, 0 < c) :
    0 < recipSum A := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  have hlt : (0 : ℚ) < 1 / (a : ℚ) := by
    have : (0 : ℚ) < (a : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos a ha
    positivity
  refine lt_of_lt_of_le hlt ?_
  refine Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun n : ℕ => (1 : ℚ) / n) ?_ ha
  intro n _
  positivity

/-! ## A.2  The ambient lcm of a finite cofactor set -/

/-- The ambient lcm of a finite set of cofactors. -/
def lcmOf (C : Finset ℕ) : ℕ := C.lcm id

@[simp] theorem lcmOf_empty : lcmOf ∅ = 1 := by simp [lcmOf]

theorem dvd_lcmOf {C : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : c ∈ C) : c ∣ lcmOf C :=
  Finset.dvd_lcm (f := id) hc

/-- The ambient lcm of a set of positive cofactors is positive. -/
theorem lcmOf_pos {C : Finset ℕ} (hpos : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) : 0 < lcmOf C := by
  classical
  induction C using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | insert a s ha ih =>
      have h1 : 0 < a := hpos a (Finset.mem_insert_self a s)
      have h2 : 0 < s.lcm id := ih (fun c hc => hpos c (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hc))
      have hne : Nat.lcm a (s.lcm id) ≠ 0 := Nat.lcm_ne_zero h1.ne' h2.ne'
      have : lcmOf (insert a s) = Nat.lcm a (s.lcm id) := by
        simp [lcmOf, Finset.lcm_insert, lcm]
      rw [this]
      exact Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hne

/-! ## A.3  The integral cofactor numerator -/

/-- The integral numerator of the reciprocal sum of `E` over the ambient lcm of `C`:
`cofactorNum C E = ∑_{c ∈ E} lcmOf C / c`, a natural number whenever `E ⊆ C`. -/
def cofactorNum (C E : Finset ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ c ∈ E, lcmOf C / c

@[simp] theorem cofactorNum_empty (C : Finset ℕ) : cofactorNum C ∅ = 0 := by
  simp [cofactorNum]

/-- **The exact compiler identity.**  For `E ⊆ C` with all cofactors positive,
`recipSum E = cofactorNum C E / lcmOf C` in `ℚ`. -/
theorem recipSum_eq_cofactorNum_div {C E : Finset ℕ} (hEC : E ⊆ C)
    (hpos : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) :
    recipSum E = ((cofactorNum C E : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  have hL : 0 < lcmOf C := lcmOf_pos hpos
  have hL' : ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast hL.ne'
  rw [eq_div_iff hL', cofactorNum]
  push_cast
  rw [recipSum_def, Finset.sum_mul]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro c hc
  have hcC : c ∈ C := hEC hc
  have hc0 : (c : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    have := hpos c hcC
    exact_mod_cast this.ne'
  have hcast : ((lcmOf C / c : ℕ) : ℚ) = ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ℚ) / (c : ℚ) :=
    Nat.cast_div (dvd_lcmOf hcC) hc0
  rw [hcast]
  field_simp

/-- On positive cofactors, a nonempty `E ⊆ C` has a nonzero integral numerator. -/
theorem cofactorNum_ne_zero {C E : Finset ℕ} (hEC : E ⊆ C) (hpos : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c)
    (hne : E.Nonempty) : cofactorNum C E ≠ 0 := by
  have hL : 0 < lcmOf C := lcmOf_pos hpos
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  have haC : a ∈ C := hEC ha
  have hdvd : a ∣ lcmOf C := dvd_lcmOf haC
  have hpa : 0 < a := hpos a haC
  have : 0 < lcmOf C / a := Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd hL hdvd) hpa
  have hle : lcmOf C / a ≤ cofactorNum C E :=
    Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun c : ℕ => lcmOf C / c) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) ha
  omega

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=3414 sha256=d32ef6f11ef6b4c07aaf0c7b5859d6dc61b4bd32379c0bae5a9eca0b16751cc1 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/CycleElimination.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.PathTransfer

/-!
# Exact elimination of isolated contact cycles

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

An *isolated cycle component* of the contact graph is a repetition-free cyclic list of contact
positions `x :: l` together with the closing contact edge `(last, x)`.  This file proves that
such a component is satisfiable exactly when the composed transfer of the path admits a pair
of endpoint values compatible with the closing relation:

`Sat ↔ ∃ a b, transfer … x l a b = true ∧ rel (last) x b a = true`,

a check over four Boolean pairs.  Cycle components are therefore *exactly decidable*.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

variable (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)

/-- The contact instance carried by the cycle through `x :: l`. -/
def cycleCSP (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)
    (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : ContactCSP :=
  { V := (x :: l).toFinset
    dom := dom
    Edges := insert (lastOf x l, x) (((x :: l).zip l).toFinset)
    rel := rel }

theorem cycleCSP_wellFormed (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : (cycleCSP dom rel x l).WellFormed := by
  intro e he
  simp only [cycleCSP, Finset.mem_insert, List.mem_toFinset] at he
  rcases he with rfl | he
  · exact ⟨by simpa [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using lastOf_mem x l,
      by simp [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset]⟩
  · have := List.of_mem_zip he
    exact ⟨by simpa [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using this.1,
      by simpa [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using List.mem_cons_of_mem x this.2⟩

/-- **`cycleCSP_sat_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Exact decision of an isolated cycle component
by the composed transfer plus the closing relation. -/
theorem cycleCSP_sat_iff (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (hnd : (x :: l).Nodup) :
    (cycleCSP dom rel x l).Sat ↔
      ∃ a b : Bool, transfer dom rel x l a b = true ∧ rel (lastOf x l) x b a = true := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hdom, hrel⟩
    have hok : chainOk dom rel x l f := by
      refine (chainOk_iff dom rel x l f).2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v hv
        exact hdom v (by simpa [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using hv)
      · intro e he
        refine hrel e ?_
        simp only [cycleCSP, Finset.mem_insert, List.mem_toFinset]
        exact Or.inr he
    have hclose : rel (lastOf x l) x (f (lastOf x l)) (f x) = true :=
      hrel (lastOf x l, x) (by simp [cycleCSP])
    exact ⟨f x, f (lastOf x l),
      (transfer_spec dom rel x l hnd _ _).2 ⟨f, rfl, rfl, hok⟩, hclose⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, htr, hclose⟩
    obtain ⟨f, hfx, hfb, hok⟩ := (transfer_spec dom rel x l hnd a b).1 htr
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := (chainOk_iff dom rel x l f).1 hok
    refine ⟨f, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      exact h1 v (by simpa [cycleCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using hv)
    · intro e he
      simp only [cycleCSP, Finset.mem_insert, List.mem_toFinset] at he
      rcases he with rfl | he
      · simpa [hfx, hfb] using hclose
      · exact h2 e he

/-- Satisfiability of an isolated cycle component is decidable by the finite four-pair
check. -/
instance decidableCycleCriterion (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) :
    Decidable (∃ a b : Bool, transfer dom rel x l a b = true ∧ rel (lastOf x l) x b a = true) :=
  inferInstance

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=6240 sha256=e81db15b6502df953577f7e75d58d0020ea5c3c245aa3011a7ec421d292cde5a path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/CycleRank.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.ForestElimination
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.CycleElimination

/-!
# Cycle rank of a contact component, and reduction to a leafless kernel

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

The *excess* (cyclomatic count) of a finite contact instance is

`excess I = |Edges| − |V| + 1`.

This file proves:

* `excess_elimLeaf` / `Peel.excess_eq`: leaf elimination preserves the excess exactly;
* `pathCSP_excess` and `cycleCSP_excess`: a contact path has excess `0`, an isolated contact
  cycle has excess `1`;
* `exists_peel_to_leafless`: every finite contact instance peels, in finitely many exact
  steps, to a **leafless** instance — the finite branching kernel — whose satisfiability is
  still exactly decidable (`ContactCSP.sat_iff_satB`).

Nothing here rejects any kernel; that global step is the `OPEN` node recorded in
`Anchored/BicyclicInterface.lean`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

namespace ContactCSP

/-- The excess (cyclomatic count) `|Edges| − |V| + 1` of a finite contact instance. -/
def excess (I : ContactCSP) : ℤ := (I.Edges.card : ℤ) - (I.V.card : ℤ) + 1

/-- **`excess_elimLeaf`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Leaf elimination removes one position and one
edge, hence preserves the excess. -/
theorem excess_elimLeaf (I : ContactCSP) {x y : ℕ} (hx : x ∈ I.V) (hedge : (x, y) ∈ I.Edges) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).excess = I.excess := by
  have h1 : (I.elimLeaf x y).V.card = I.V.card - 1 := by
    simpa [elimLeaf] using Finset.card_erase_of_mem hx
  have h2 : (I.elimLeaf x y).Edges.card = I.Edges.card - 1 := by
    simpa [elimLeaf] using Finset.card_erase_of_mem hedge
  have hxpos : 1 ≤ I.V.card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hepos : 1 ≤ I.Edges.card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨(x, y), hedge⟩
  simp only [excess, h1, h2]
  omega

/-- Peeling preserves the excess. -/
theorem Peel.excess_eq {I J : ContactCSP} (h : Peel I J) : J.excess = I.excess := by
  induction h with
  | refl I => rfl
  | step x y hx hy hxy hedge hiso _ ih =>
      rw [ih, excess_elimLeaf _ hx hedge]

/-! ## A.18  Excess of paths and isolated cycles -/

theorem zip_nodup_of_left : ∀ (l₁ l₂ : List ℕ), l₁.Nodup → (l₁.zip l₂).Nodup := by
  intro l₁
  induction l₁ with
  | nil => intro l₂ _; simp
  | cons a t ih =>
      intro l₂ h
      cases l₂ with
      | nil => simp
      | cons b s =>
          rw [List.zip_cons_cons]
          refine List.nodup_cons.2 ⟨?_, ih s (List.nodup_cons.1 h).2⟩
          intro hmem
          exact (List.nodup_cons.1 h).1 (List.of_mem_zip hmem).1

/-- A contact path has excess `0`. -/
theorem pathCSP_excess (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)
    (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (hnd : (x :: l).Nodup) : (pathCSP dom rel x l).excess = 0 := by
  have hV : (pathCSP dom rel x l).V.card = l.length + 1 := by
    rw [show (pathCSP dom rel x l).V = (x :: l).toFinset from rfl,
      List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd]
    simp
  have hE : (pathCSP dom rel x l).Edges.card = l.length := by
    have hnd' : ((x :: l).zip l).Nodup := zip_nodup_of_left _ _ hnd
    rw [show (pathCSP dom rel x l).Edges = ((x :: l).zip l).toFinset from rfl,
      List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd']
    simp [List.length_zip]
  simp only [excess, hV, hE]
  omega

/-- An isolated contact cycle has excess `1`. -/
theorem cycleCSP_excess (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)
    (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (hnd : (x :: l).Nodup) : (cycleCSP dom rel x l).excess = 1 := by
  have hV : (cycleCSP dom rel x l).V.card = l.length + 1 := by
    rw [show (cycleCSP dom rel x l).V = (x :: l).toFinset from rfl,
      List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd]
    simp
  have hnd' : ((x :: l).zip l).Nodup := zip_nodup_of_left _ _ hnd
  have hnotmem : (lastOf x l, x) ∉ ((x :: l).zip l).toFinset := by
    intro hmem
    rw [List.mem_toFinset] at hmem
    have hx : x ∈ l := (List.of_mem_zip hmem).2
    exact (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).1 hx
  have hE : (cycleCSP dom rel x l).Edges.card = l.length + 1 := by
    rw [show (cycleCSP dom rel x l).Edges
        = insert (lastOf x l, x) (((x :: l).zip l).toFinset) from rfl,
      Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hnotmem, List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd']
    simp [List.length_zip]
  simp only [excess, hV, hE]
  omega

/-! ## A.19  Reduction to the finite leafless kernel -/

/-- `x` is an eliminable leaf of `I`, with unique contact edge `(x, y)`. -/
def IsLeafWith (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) : Prop :=
  x ∈ I.V ∧ y ∈ I.V ∧ x ≠ y ∧ (x, y) ∈ I.Edges ∧
    ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, e ≠ (x, y) → e.1 ≠ x ∧ e.2 ≠ x

/-- An instance with no eliminable leaf: the finite branching kernel of the component. -/
def Leafless (I : ContactCSP) : Prop := ¬ ∃ x y : ℕ, IsLeafWith I x y

/-- **`exists_peel_to_leafless`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every finite contact instance reduces,
by finitely many exact leaf eliminations, to a leafless instance (a finite branching kernel),
with satisfiability preserved at every step. -/
theorem exists_peel_to_leafless (I : ContactCSP) : ∃ J, Peel I J ∧ Leafless J := by
  classical
  generalize hn : I.Edges.card = n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing I with
  | _ n ih =>
      by_cases hleaf : ∃ x y : ℕ, IsLeafWith I x y
      · obtain ⟨x, y, hx, hy, hxy, hedge, hiso⟩ := hleaf
        have hlt : (I.elimLeaf x y).Edges.card < n := by
          rw [← hn]
          exact elimLeaf_edges_card_lt I hedge
        obtain ⟨J, hJ, hJleaf⟩ := ih _ hlt (I.elimLeaf x y) rfl
        exact ⟨J, Peel.step x y hx hy hxy hedge hiso hJ, hJleaf⟩
      · exact ⟨I, Peel.refl I, hleaf⟩

/-- The reduction of `exists_peel_to_leafless` is satisfiability-exact, and the resulting
finite kernel is itself exactly decidable. -/
theorem peel_to_leafless_decidable (I : ContactCSP) :
    ∃ J, Peel I J ∧ Leafless J ∧ (I.Sat ↔ J.Sat) ∧
      (J.WellFormed → (J.Sat ↔ J.satB = true)) := by
  obtain ⟨J, hJ, hJl⟩ := exists_peel_to_leafless I
  exact ⟨J, hJ, hJl, hJ.sat_iff, fun hwf => J.sat_iff_satB hwf⟩

end ContactCSP

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=3422 sha256=7dfad755d9d648c7d782051633e236d3312ce34bb9bdce1e1fe8a8569df61f04 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/Fingerprint.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.ReciprocalState

/-!
# The finite anchored fingerprint

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

For a finite anchored state `(C, P, N)` the *fingerprint* is the finite integer product

`F_C(P,N) = ∏_{v ∈ 𝒱_C(P,N), v > 0} num v`,

taken over the strictly positive permitted values only; the zero value is handled separately
and is never encoded as a numerator.  The main theorem is the exact equivalence

`AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔ (zero state allowed) ∨ p ∣ F_C(P,N)`,

valid for every prime `p`.  **No claim whatsoever is made about the size of `F`** — it is a
finite integer, and no asymptotic statement about it occurs anywhere in this namespace.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-- The strictly positive permitted values. -/
def positiveValues (C P N : Finset ℕ) : Finset ℚ :=
  (valueSet C P N).filter (fun v => 0 < v)

@[simp] theorem mem_positiveValues {C P N : Finset ℕ} {v : ℚ} :
    v ∈ positiveValues C P N ↔ v ∈ valueSet C P N ∧ 0 < v := by
  simp [positiveValues]

/-- The finite anchored fingerprint `F_C(P,N)`. -/
def fingerprint (C P N : Finset ℕ) : ℤ := ∏ v ∈ positiveValues C P N, v.num

/-- **`anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact finite criterion:
local feasibility holds iff the zero state is allowed or `p` divides the fingerprint. -/
theorem anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (C P N : Finset ℕ) :
    AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔
      ((0 : ℚ) ∈ valueSet C P N) ∨ (p : ℤ) ∣ fingerprint C P N := by
  have hpZ : Prime ((p : ℤ)) := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.mp hp.out
  rw [anchoredFeasible_iff_num]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact Or.inl (mem_valueSet.2 ⟨E, hE, h⟩)
    · by_cases h0 : recipSum E = 0
      · exact Or.inl (mem_valueSet.2 ⟨E, hE, h0⟩)
      · refine Or.inr ?_
        have hmem : recipSum E ∈ positiveValues C P N :=
          mem_positiveValues.2 ⟨mem_valueSet.2 ⟨E, hE, rfl⟩,
            lt_of_le_of_ne (recipSum_nonneg E) (Ne.symm h0)⟩
        exact dvd_trans h (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem (fun v : ℚ => v.num) hmem)
  · rintro (h | h)
    · obtain ⟨E, hE, hE0⟩ := mem_valueSet.1 h
      exact ⟨E, hE, Or.inl hE0⟩
    · rw [fingerprint, hpZ.dvd_finset_prod_iff] at h
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hdvd⟩ := h
      obtain ⟨hvmem, _⟩ := mem_positiveValues.1 hv
      obtain ⟨E, hE, hEv⟩ := mem_valueSet.1 hvmem
      exact ⟨E, hE, Or.inr (by rw [hEv]; exact hdvd)⟩

/-- The fingerprint criterion makes local feasibility *exactly decidable*: the right-hand
side is a finite, purely arithmetic condition. -/
instance decidableAnchoredFeasible (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C P N : Finset ℕ) :
    Decidable (AnchoredFeasible p C P N) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ (anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint p C P N).symm

/-- With positive cofactors the zero state is allowed exactly when `P = ∅`, so the criterion
takes the fully explicit form used downstream. -/
theorem anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint_of_pos (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {C P N : Finset ℕ}
    (hC : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) :
    AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔ (P = ∅ ∨ (p : ℤ) ∣ fingerprint C P N) := by
  rw [anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint p C P N, zero_mem_valueSet_iff hC]

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=7453 sha256=44aaedd33deab26c2a05c3e1b8fbe28edc86ee2bf3d38e39724bb18ddcaad7cf path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/ForestElimination.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.ContactGraph

/-!
# Exact leaf elimination on the contact graph (forest components)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

A *leaf* of the contact graph is a position `x` occurring in exactly one contact edge
`(x, y)`.  Eliminating it means deleting `x` and the edge, and intersecting the unary domain
at `y` with the projection of the local relation.  This file proves:

* `sat_elimLeaf_iff`: leaf elimination preserves satisfiability **exactly** (both directions);
* `elimLeaf_edges_card_lt`: each elimination strictly decreases the number of contact edges,
  so the process terminates;
* `Peel.sat_iff` and `forest_decision`: a component that peels to an edgeless instance — i.e.
  a forest component — is satisfiable exactly when every remaining unary domain is nonempty.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

namespace ContactCSP

/-- Eliminate the leaf `x`, whose only contact edge is `(x, y)`. -/
def elimLeaf (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) : ContactCSP :=
  { V := I.V.erase x
    dom := fun v b =>
      if v = y then
        I.dom v b && ((I.dom x false && I.rel x y false b) || (I.dom x true && I.rel x y true b))
      else I.dom v b
    Edges := I.Edges.erase (x, y)
    rel := I.rel }

@[simp] theorem elimLeaf_V (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) : (I.elimLeaf x y).V = I.V.erase x := rfl

@[simp] theorem elimLeaf_Edges (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).Edges = I.Edges.erase (x, y) := rfl

@[simp] theorem elimLeaf_rel (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) : (I.elimLeaf x y).rel = I.rel := rfl

theorem elimLeaf_dom (I : ContactCSP) (x y v : ℕ) (b : Bool) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).dom v b =
      (if v = y then
        I.dom v b && ((I.dom x false && I.rel x y false b) || (I.dom x true && I.rel x y true b))
      else I.dom v b) := rfl

theorem elimLeaf_dom_of_ne (I : ContactCSP) {x y v : ℕ} (h : v ≠ y) (b : Bool) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).dom v b = I.dom v b := by
  rw [elimLeaf_dom, if_neg h]

theorem elimLeaf_dom_self (I : ContactCSP) (x y : ℕ) (b : Bool) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).dom y b =
      (I.dom y b && ((I.dom x false && I.rel x y false b) ||
        (I.dom x true && I.rel x y true b))) := by
  rw [elimLeaf_dom, if_pos rfl]

theorem elimLeaf_wellFormed {I : ContactCSP} {x y : ℕ} (hwf : I.WellFormed)
    (hiso : ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, e ≠ (x, y) → e.1 ≠ x ∧ e.2 ≠ x) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).WellFormed := by
  intro e he
  rw [elimLeaf_Edges, Finset.mem_erase] at he
  obtain ⟨hne, hmem⟩ := he
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hwf e hmem
  obtain ⟨k1, k2⟩ := hiso e hmem hne
  exact ⟨by rw [elimLeaf_V]; exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨k1, h1⟩,
    by rw [elimLeaf_V]; exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨k2, h2⟩⟩

/-- **`sat_elimLeaf_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Leaf elimination preserves satisfiability
exactly. -/
theorem sat_elimLeaf_iff (I : ContactCSP) {x y : ℕ} (hx : x ∈ I.V) (hy : y ∈ I.V)
    (hxy : x ≠ y) (hedge : (x, y) ∈ I.Edges)
    (hiso : ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, e ≠ (x, y) → e.1 ≠ x ∧ e.2 ≠ x) :
    I.Sat ↔ (I.elimLeaf x y).Sat := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hdom, hrel⟩
    refine ⟨f, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      rw [elimLeaf_V, Finset.mem_erase] at hv
      have hvV : v ∈ I.V := hv.2
      by_cases hvy : v = y
      · subst hvy
        have h1 : I.dom v (f v) = true := hdom v hvV
        have h2 : I.rel x v (f x) (f v) = true := hrel (x, v) hedge
        have h3 : I.dom x (f x) = true := hdom x hx
        rw [elimLeaf_dom_self, Bool.and_eq_true]
        refine ⟨h1, ?_⟩
        rw [Bool.or_eq_true]
        rcases hfx : f x with _ | _
        · rw [hfx] at h2 h3
          exact Or.inl (by rw [Bool.and_eq_true]; exact ⟨h3, h2⟩)
        · rw [hfx] at h2 h3
          exact Or.inr (by rw [Bool.and_eq_true]; exact ⟨h3, h2⟩)
      · rw [elimLeaf_dom_of_ne I hvy]
        exact hdom v hvV
    · intro e he
      rw [elimLeaf_rel]
      rw [elimLeaf_Edges] at he
      exact hrel e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)
  · rintro ⟨g, hdom, hrel⟩
    have hyV : y ∈ (I.elimLeaf x y).V := by
      rw [elimLeaf_V]
      exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hxy h.symm, hy⟩
    have hgy := hdom y hyV
    rw [elimLeaf_dom_self, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true] at hgy
    obtain ⟨hgdom, hgc⟩ := hgy
    obtain ⟨c, hcx, hcrel⟩ : ∃ c : Bool, I.dom x c = true ∧ I.rel x y c (g y) = true := by
      rcases hgc with h | h
      · rw [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact ⟨false, h.1, h.2⟩
      · rw [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact ⟨true, h.1, h.2⟩
    refine ⟨Function.update g x c, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      by_cases hvx : v = x
      · subst hvx
        simpa using hcx
      · have hv' : v ∈ (I.elimLeaf x y).V := by
          rw [elimLeaf_V]
          exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hvx, hv⟩
        have hgv := hdom v hv'
        rw [Function.update_of_ne hvx]
        by_cases hvy : v = y
        · subst hvy
          rw [elimLeaf_dom_self, Bool.and_eq_true] at hgv
          exact hgv.1
        · rw [elimLeaf_dom_of_ne I hvy] at hgv
          exact hgv
    · intro e he
      by_cases hexy : e = (x, y)
      · subst hexy
        have k1 : Function.update g x c (x, y).1 = c := by simp
        have k2 : Function.update g x c (x, y).2 = g y := by
          simp [Function.update_of_ne (show (x, y).2 ≠ x from fun h => hxy h.symm)]
        rw [k1, k2]
        exact hcrel
      · obtain ⟨k1, k2⟩ := hiso e he hexy
        have he' : e ∈ (I.elimLeaf x y).Edges := by
          rw [elimLeaf_Edges]
          exact Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hexy, he⟩
        have hge := hrel e he'
        rw [elimLeaf_rel] at hge
        rw [Function.update_of_ne k1, Function.update_of_ne k2]
        exact hge

/-- Each leaf elimination strictly decreases the number of contact edges. -/
theorem elimLeaf_edges_card_lt (I : ContactCSP) {x y : ℕ} (hedge : (x, y) ∈ I.Edges) :
    (I.elimLeaf x y).Edges.card < I.Edges.card := by
  rw [elimLeaf_Edges]
  exact Finset.card_erase_lt_of_mem hedge

/-! ## A.17  Iterated peeling -/

/-- `Peel I J`: the instance `J` is obtained from `I` by a finite sequence of exact leaf
eliminations. -/
inductive Peel : ContactCSP → ContactCSP → Prop
  /-- the empty sequence -/
  | refl (I : ContactCSP) : Peel I I
  /-- one exact leaf elimination, followed by a peel -/
  | step {I J : ContactCSP} (x y : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ I.V) (hy : y ∈ I.V) (hxy : x ≠ y)
      (hedge : (x, y) ∈ I.Edges)
      (hiso : ∀ e ∈ I.Edges, e ≠ (x, y) → e.1 ≠ x ∧ e.2 ≠ x)
      (h : Peel (I.elimLeaf x y) J) : Peel I J

/-- **`Peel.sat_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Peeling preserves satisfiability exactly. -/
theorem Peel.sat_iff {I J : ContactCSP} (h : Peel I J) : I.Sat ↔ J.Sat := by
  induction h with
  | refl I => exact Iff.rfl
  | step x y hx hy hxy hedge hiso _ ih =>
      exact (sat_elimLeaf_iff _ hx hy hxy hedge hiso).trans ih

/-- **`forest_decision`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A component that peels to an edgeless instance
(a forest component) is satisfiable exactly when every surviving unary domain is nonempty.
This is an exact, finite decision. -/
theorem forest_decision {I J : ContactCSP} (h : Peel I J) (hJ : J.Edges = ∅) :
    I.Sat ↔ ∀ v ∈ J.V, ∃ b : Bool, J.dom v b = true :=
  (h.sat_iff).trans (J.sat_iff_domains_nonempty_of_no_edges hJ)

end ContactCSP

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=7731 sha256=54bcda6cef45d075e86b18daa446b923abeebb2605670ce15eddc56e7cd4c97d path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/PathTransfer.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.ContactGraph

/-!
# Exact transfer along a contact path

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

A *contact path* is a repetition-free list of contact positions `x :: l`, carrying the unary
domains `dom` and the binary contact relations `rel` of the contact graph.  This file defines
the exact Boolean transfer `transfer dom rel x l a b` (composition of the local relations
along the path) and proves

* `transfer_spec`: `transfer … a b = true` iff there is a global assignment with the two
  prescribed endpoint values satisfying every local condition along the path;
* `pathCSP_sat_iff`: satisfiability of the path instance is exactly
  `∃ a b, transfer … a b = true`, a check over four Boolean pairs.

Everything is exact and finite; no approximation of any kind is used.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-- The last vertex of the path `x :: l`. -/
def lastOf : ℕ → List ℕ → ℕ
  | x, [] => x
  | _, (y :: t) => lastOf y t

theorem lastOf_mem (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : lastOf x l ∈ x :: l := by
  induction l generalizing x with
  | nil => simp [lastOf]
  | cons y t ih =>
      have := ih y
      simp [lastOf] at *
      tauto

/-- The assignment `f` satisfies every local condition along the path `x :: l`. -/
def chainOk (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool) :
    ℕ → List ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → Prop
  | x, [], f => dom x (f x) = true
  | x, (y :: t), f => dom x (f x) = true ∧ rel x y (f x) (f y) = true ∧ chainOk dom rel y t f

/-- The exact Boolean transfer along the path `x :: l`. -/
def transfer (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool) :
    ℕ → List ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool
  | x, [], a, b => dom x a && (a == b)
  | x, (y :: t), a, b =>
      dom x a && ((rel x y a false && transfer dom rel y t false b) ||
        (rel x y a true && transfer dom rel y t true b))

variable (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)

theorem chainOk_congr {f g : ℕ → Bool} (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ)
    (h : ∀ z ∈ x :: l, f z = g z) : chainOk dom rel x l f ↔ chainOk dom rel x l g := by
  induction l generalizing x with
  | nil => simp [chainOk, h x (by simp)]
  | cons y t ih =>
      have hx : f x = g x := h x (by simp)
      have hy : f y = g y := h y (by simp)
      have ht : ∀ z ∈ y :: t, f z = g z := by
        intro z hz
        exact h z (by simp at hz ⊢; tauto)
      simp [chainOk, hx, hy, ih y ht]

/-- Local path conditions, unpacked as vertex conditions and edge conditions. -/
theorem chainOk_iff (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (f : ℕ → Bool) :
    chainOk dom rel x l f ↔
      ((∀ v ∈ x :: l, dom v (f v) = true) ∧
        (∀ e ∈ (x :: l).zip l, rel e.1 e.2 (f e.1) (f e.2) = true)) := by
  induction l generalizing x with
  | nil => simp [chainOk]
  | cons y t ih =>
      simp only [chainOk, ih y, List.zip_cons_cons, List.mem_cons]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
        refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
        · rintro v (rfl | hv)
          · exact h1
          · exact h3 v hv
        · rintro e (rfl | he)
          · exact h2
          · exact h4 e he
      · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
        exact ⟨h1 x (Or.inl rfl), h2 (x, y) (Or.inl rfl),
          fun v hv => h1 v (Or.inr hv), fun e he => h2 e (Or.inr he)⟩

/-- **`transfer_spec`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The Boolean transfer is exactly the existence of a
path assignment with the prescribed endpoint values. -/
theorem transfer_spec (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (hnd : (x :: l).Nodup) (a b : Bool) :
    transfer dom rel x l a b = true ↔
      ∃ f : ℕ → Bool, f x = a ∧ f (lastOf x l) = b ∧ chainOk dom rel x l f := by
  induction l generalizing x a with
  | nil =>
      simp only [transfer, lastOf, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hd, hab⟩
        exact ⟨fun _ => a, rfl, hab ▸ rfl, by simpa [chainOk] using hd⟩
      · rintro ⟨f, hfx, hfb, hok⟩
        refine ⟨by rw [← hfx]; simpa [chainOk] using hok, by rw [← hfx, hfb]⟩
  | cons y t ih =>
      have hxnotin : x ∉ y :: t := by
        simpa using (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).1
      have hndt : (y :: t).Nodup := (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).2
      simp only [transfer, lastOf, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hd, hc⟩
        have hex : ∃ c : Bool, rel x y a c = true ∧ transfer dom rel y t c b = true := by
          rcases hc with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
          · exact ⟨false, h1, h2⟩
          · exact ⟨true, h1, h2⟩
        obtain ⟨c, hrel, htr⟩ := hex
        obtain ⟨g, hgy, hgb, hgok⟩ := (ih y hndt c).1 htr
        refine ⟨Function.update g x a, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
        · have hne : lastOf y t ≠ x := by
            intro h
            exact hxnotin (h ▸ lastOf_mem y t)
          simpa [Function.update_of_ne hne] using hgb
        · have hupd : ∀ z ∈ y :: t, Function.update g x a z = g z := by
            intro z hz
            have : z ≠ x := by rintro rfl; exact hxnotin hz
            simp [Function.update_of_ne this]
          refine ⟨by simpa using hd, ?_, ?_⟩
          · have h1 : Function.update g x a y = g y := hupd y (by simp)
            simp [h1, hgy, hrel]
          · exact (chainOk_congr dom rel y t (fun z hz => (hupd z hz).symm)).1 hgok
      · rintro ⟨f, hfx, hfb, hok⟩
        obtain ⟨hd, hrel, hrest⟩ := hok
        have htr : transfer dom rel y t (f y) b = true :=
          (ih y hndt (f y)).2 ⟨f, rfl, hfb, hrest⟩
        refine ⟨by rw [← hfx]; exact hd, ?_⟩
        rcases hfy : f y with _ | _
        · rw [hfy] at hrel htr
          exact Or.inl ⟨by rw [← hfx]; exact hrel, htr⟩
        · rw [hfy] at hrel htr
          exact Or.inr ⟨by rw [← hfx]; exact hrel, htr⟩

/-! ## A.15  The path instance of the contact graph -/

/-- The contact instance carried by the path `x :: l`. -/
def pathCSP (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool)
    (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : ContactCSP :=
  { V := (x :: l).toFinset
    dom := dom
    Edges := ((x :: l).zip l).toFinset
    rel := rel }

theorem pathCSP_wellFormed (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : (pathCSP dom rel x l).WellFormed := by
  intro e he
  simp only [pathCSP, List.mem_toFinset] at he ⊢
  have hz := List.of_mem_zip he
  exact ⟨hz.1, List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hz.2⟩

/-- **`pathCSP_sat_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A contact path component is satisfiable exactly
when the composed transfer admits a pair of endpoint values — a check over four Boolean
pairs, hence exactly decidable. -/
theorem pathCSP_sat_iff (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) (hnd : (x :: l).Nodup) :
    (pathCSP dom rel x l).Sat ↔ ∃ a b : Bool, transfer dom rel x l a b = true := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hdom, hrel⟩
    have hok : chainOk dom rel x l f := by
      refine (chainOk_iff dom rel x l f).2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v hv
        exact hdom v (by simpa [pathCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using hv)
      · intro e he
        exact hrel e (by simpa [pathCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using he)
    exact ⟨f x, f (lastOf x l), (transfer_spec dom rel x l hnd _ _).2 ⟨f, rfl, rfl, hok⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, htr⟩
    obtain ⟨f, -, -, hok⟩ := (transfer_spec dom rel x l hnd a b).1 htr
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := (chainOk_iff dom rel x l f).1 hok
    refine ⟨f, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      exact h1 v (by simpa [pathCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using hv)
    · intro e he
      exact h2 e (by simpa [pathCSP, List.mem_toFinset] using he)

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=7500 sha256=8473cd4fe1c143400d33fb4785d96a87dcdff6d90a92b42ffe1b5fa4ea019fda path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/PrimePowerLayer.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.Fingerprint

/-!
# The full prime-power layer condition

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Fix a prime `p`, a threshold power `q = p ^ a` and a window `[a₀, M]`.  The *actual* cofactor
set of the layer is

`C = { c : a₀ ≤ q * c ≤ M }`,

`L = lcm C`, and `t = v_p(L)`.  This file proves the exact equivalence between

* the **full top prime-power condition** `p ^ (t + 1) ∣ ∑_{c ∈ E} L / c`, and
* the anchored reciprocal condition `v_p(∑_{c ∈ E} 1/c) ≥ 1`,

for every nonempty `E ⊆ C`, with **no** coprimality assumption: the case `p ∣ c` is retained
and is exhibited by an explicit witness (`layer_retains_p_dvd_cofactor`).  The reduction to
the leading-digit / unit-cofactor special case is *not* performed — that firewall is the
point of this module.

The empty subset is a genuine exception and is recorded as such
(`layer_condition_empty_firewall`), which is why the equivalence carries a nonemptiness
hypothesis.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-! ## A.7  A computation helper for `p`-adic valuations of explicit numbers -/

/-- `padicValNat p n = k` from the two explicit divisibility facts. -/
theorem padicValNat_eq_of_dvd_of_not_dvd {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {n k : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (h1 : p ^ k ∣ n) (h2 : ¬ p ^ (k + 1) ∣ n) : padicValNat p n = k := by
  have a1 := (padicValNat_dvd_iff_le hn).1 h1
  have a2 : ¬ (k + 1 ≤ padicValNat p n) := fun h => h2 ((padicValNat_dvd_iff_le hn).2 h)
  omega

/-! ## A.8  The layer cofactor set -/

/-- The cofactor set of the `q`-layer inside the window `[a₀, M]`:
`layerCofactors q a₀ M = { c : a₀ ≤ q * c ≤ M }`. -/
def layerCofactors (q a₀ M : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 M).filter (fun c => a₀ ≤ q * c ∧ q * c ≤ M)

@[simp] theorem mem_layerCofactors {q a₀ M c : ℕ} :
    c ∈ layerCofactors q a₀ M ↔ (1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ M) ∧ (a₀ ≤ q * c ∧ q * c ≤ M) := by
  simp [layerCofactors, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, and_assoc]

/-- Every layer cofactor is positive. -/
theorem layerCofactors_pos {q a₀ M : ℕ} : ∀ c ∈ layerCofactors q a₀ M, 0 < c := by
  intro c hc
  have := (mem_layerCofactors.1 hc).1.1
  omega

/-! ## A.9  The exact prime-power / reciprocal equivalence -/

/-- **`layer_primePower_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For a finite set `C` of positive cofactors,
`L = lcmOf C`, `t = v_p(L)` and a nonempty `E ⊆ C`:

`p ^ (t + 1) ∣ ∑_{c ∈ E} L / c  ↔  v_p(∑_{c ∈ E} 1/c) ≥ 1`.

No hypothesis relates `p` to the elements of `C`; in particular cofactors divisible by `p`
are retained. -/
theorem layer_primePower_iff (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {C E : Finset ℕ} (hEC : E ⊆ C)
    (hC : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) (hne : E.Nonempty) :
    p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) ∣ cofactorNum C E ↔
      1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum E) := by
  have hL : 0 < lcmOf C := lcmOf_pos hC
  have hS : cofactorNum C E ≠ 0 := cofactorNum_ne_zero hEC hC hne
  have hrec : recipSum E = ((cofactorNum C E : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ℚ) :=
    recipSum_eq_cofactorNum_div hEC hC
  have hSq : ((cofactorNum C E : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hS
  have hLq : ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hL.ne'
  have hval : padicValRat p (recipSum E)
      = (padicValNat p (cofactorNum C E) : ℤ) - (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) : ℤ) := by
    rw [hrec, padicValRat.div hSq hLq, padicValRat.of_nat, padicValRat.of_nat]
  rw [hval, padicValNat_dvd_iff_le hS]
  omega

/-- The same statement with the layer numerator written as an integer sum. -/
theorem layer_primePower_iff_int (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {C E : Finset ℕ} (hEC : E ⊆ C)
    (hC : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) (hne : E.Nonempty) :
    ((p : ℤ) ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) ∣ ∑ c ∈ E, ((lcmOf C / c : ℕ) : ℤ)) ↔
      1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum E) := by
  rw [← layer_primePower_iff p hEC hC hne]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have : ((p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ ((cofactorNum C E : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      push_cast
      simpa [cofactorNum, Nat.cast_sum] using h
    exact_mod_cast this
  · intro h
    have : ((p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ ((cofactorNum C E : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      exact_mod_cast h
    push_cast at this
    simpa [cofactorNum, Nat.cast_sum] using this

/-- **`anchoredFeasible_iff_layer_primePower`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The anchored local
feasibility predicate is exactly the full prime-power layer condition over the allowed
subsets, the zero state appearing explicitly as `E = ∅`. -/
theorem anchoredFeasible_iff_layer_primePower (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {C P N : Finset ℕ}
    (hC : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) :
    AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔
      ∃ E ∈ allowed C P N,
        E = ∅ ∨ p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) ∣ cofactorNum C E := by
  unfold AnchoredFeasible
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    refine ⟨E, hE, ?_⟩
    rcases Finset.eq_empty_or_nonempty E with hE0 | hne
    · exact Or.inl hE0
    · have hEC : E ⊆ C := (mem_allowed.1 hE).2.1
      have hpos : 0 < recipSum E := recipSum_pos hne (fun c hc => hC c (hEC hc))
      rcases h with h | h
      · exact absurd h hpos.ne'
      · exact Or.inr ((layer_primePower_iff p hEC hC hne).2 h)
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    refine ⟨E, hE, ?_⟩
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact Or.inl (by simp [h])
    · rcases Finset.eq_empty_or_nonempty E with hE0 | hne
      · exact Or.inl (by simp [hE0])
      · have hEC : E ⊆ C := (mem_allowed.1 hE).2.1
        exact Or.inr ((layer_primePower_iff p hEC hC hne).1 h)

/-! ## A.10  Firewalls -/

/-- **`layer_condition_empty_firewall`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The nonemptiness hypothesis of
`layer_primePower_iff` is necessary: for `E = ∅` the divisibility holds trivially while the
valuation condition fails (`v_p(0) = 0` by convention). -/
theorem layer_condition_empty_firewall (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C : Finset ℕ) :
    p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) ∣ cofactorNum C ∅ ∧
      ¬ (1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum (∅ : Finset ℕ))) := by
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
  simp [recipSum]

/-- **`layer_retains_p_dvd_cofactor`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  An explicit witness in which the
selected cofactors are themselves divisible by `p`: with `C = {2,3,6}`, `E = {2,6}` and
`p = 2` the full prime-power condition holds, hence so does the valuation condition.  The
layer condition therefore genuinely covers the case `p ∣ c`, and is *not* reduced to the
unit-cofactor special case. -/
theorem layer_retains_p_dvd_cofactor :
    lcmOf {2, 3, 6} = 6 ∧ cofactorNum {2, 3, 6} {2, 6} = 4 ∧
      (2 ∣ (2 : ℕ) ∧ 2 ∣ (6 : ℕ)) ∧
      1 ≤ padicValRat 2 (recipSum {2, 6}) := by
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  have hlcm : lcmOf {2, 3, 6} = 6 := by decide
  have hnum : cofactorNum {2, 3, 6} {2, 6} = 4 := by decide
  have ht : padicValNat 2 (lcmOf {2, 3, 6}) = 1 := by
    rw [hlcm]
    exact padicValNat_eq_of_dvd_of_not_dvd (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  have hEC : ({2, 6} : Finset ℕ) ⊆ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ) := by decide
  have hC : ∀ c ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), 0 < c := by decide
  have hne : ({2, 6} : Finset ℕ).Nonempty := ⟨2, by decide⟩
  refine ⟨hlcm, hnum, ⟨⟨1, rfl⟩, ⟨3, rfl⟩⟩, ?_⟩
  refine (layer_primePower_iff 2 hEC hC hne).1 ?_
  rw [ht, hnum]
  norm_num

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5610 sha256=a18907455469325ae82c7d969c5a4b828fe9ca79425a3ca199e55f7545e529dc path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/ReciprocalState.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.Core

/-!
# Anchored finite reciprocal state

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Let `C` be a finite set of positive cofactors, `P ⊆ C` the *mandatory selected* cofactors and
`N ⊆ C` the *mandatory omitted* cofactors, with `P ∩ N = ∅`.  The permitted reciprocal-value
set is

`𝒱_C(P,N) = { ∑_{c ∈ E} 1/c : P ⊆ E ⊆ C \ N }`,

computed in exact rational arithmetic.  The empty subset (value `0`) is represented
explicitly and is *never* encoded by a numerator product.

The local feasibility predicate `AnchoredFeasible p C P N` says that some allowed subset has
`p`-adic valuation at least `1`, with the zero value treated separately.

The file proves the exact reduced-numerator criterion

`v ≠ 0 → (1 ≤ v_p(v) ↔ p ∣ num v)`

for **every** prime `p` (no largeness assumption of any kind).
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-! ## A.4  The anchored state -/

/-- An *anchor* on the cofactor set `C`: mandatory selections `P`, mandatory omissions `N`,
disjoint. -/
structure Anchor (C : Finset ℕ) (P N : Finset ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- the mandatory selections lie in `C` -/
  sel_sub : P ⊆ C
  /-- the mandatory omissions lie in `C` -/
  omit_sub : N ⊆ C
  /-- and they are disjoint -/
  disj : Disjoint P N

/-- The subsets of `C` allowed by the anchor `(P, N)`. -/
def allowed (C P N : Finset ℕ) : Finset (Finset ℕ) :=
  (C \ N).powerset.filter (fun E => P ⊆ E)

@[simp] theorem mem_allowed {C P N E : Finset ℕ} :
    E ∈ allowed C P N ↔ P ⊆ E ∧ E ⊆ C ∧ Disjoint E N := by
  classical
  simp only [allowed, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset, Finset.subset_sdiff]
  tauto

theorem allowed_nonempty {C P N : Finset ℕ} (h : Anchor C P N) :
    (allowed C P N).Nonempty :=
  ⟨P, mem_allowed.2 ⟨Finset.Subset.refl P, h.sel_sub, h.disj⟩⟩

/-- The permitted reciprocal-value set `𝒱_C(P,N)`, in exact rational arithmetic. -/
def valueSet (C P N : Finset ℕ) : Finset ℚ := (allowed C P N).image recipSum

@[simp] theorem mem_valueSet {C P N : Finset ℕ} {v : ℚ} :
    v ∈ valueSet C P N ↔ ∃ E ∈ allowed C P N, recipSum E = v := by
  simp [valueSet]

theorem valueSet_nonneg {C P N : Finset ℕ} {v : ℚ} (hv : v ∈ valueSet C P N) : 0 ≤ v := by
  obtain ⟨E, _, hE⟩ := mem_valueSet.1 hv
  exact hE ▸ recipSum_nonneg E

/-- The *zero state* is allowed exactly when nothing is mandatorily selected (given positive
cofactors).  The zero value is thus represented explicitly, never through a numerator. -/
theorem zero_mem_valueSet_iff {C P N : Finset ℕ} (hC : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) :
    (0 : ℚ) ∈ valueSet C P N ↔ P = ∅ := by
  constructor
  · rintro hv
    obtain ⟨E, hE, hE0⟩ := mem_valueSet.1 hv
    rw [mem_allowed] at hE
    by_contra hP
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.2 hP
    have haE : a ∈ E := hE.1 ha
    have : 0 < recipSum E :=
      recipSum_pos ⟨a, haE⟩ (fun c hc => hC c (hE.2.1 hc))
    rw [hE0] at this
    exact lt_irrefl _ this
  · intro hP
    refine mem_valueSet.2 ⟨∅, mem_allowed.2 ⟨by simp [hP], by simp, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
    simp

/-! ## A.5  The exact reduced-numerator criterion -/

/-- **`one_le_padicValRat_iff_dvd_num`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For a nonzero rational `v` in
lowest terms and *any* prime `p`:  `v_p(v) ≥ 1 ↔ p ∣ num v`.  No largeness hypothesis on `p`
is used. -/
theorem one_le_padicValRat_iff_dvd_num (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {v : ℚ} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    1 ≤ padicValRat p v ↔ (p : ℤ) ∣ v.num := by
  have hnum : v.num ≠ 0 := Rat.num_ne_zero.mpr hv
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hnd
    have h0 : padicValInt p v.num = 0 := padicValInt.eq_zero_of_not_dvd hnd
    have hval : padicValRat p v = -(padicValNat p v.den : ℤ) := by
      simp [padicValRat, h0]
    omega
  · intro h
    have habs : p ∣ v.num.natAbs := by
      have := Int.natAbs_dvd_natAbs.mpr h
      simpa using this
    have hd : ¬ p ∣ v.den := by
      intro hdvd
      have hcop := v.reduced
      have := Nat.Coprime.eq_one_of_dvd (Nat.Coprime.coprime_dvd_left habs hcop) hdvd
      exact hp.out.one_lt.ne' this
    have h0 : padicValNat p v.den = 0 := padicValNat.eq_zero_of_not_dvd hd
    have h1 : 1 ≤ padicValInt p v.num :=
      one_le_padicValNat_of_dvd (Int.natAbs_ne_zero.mpr hnum) habs
    simp only [padicValRat, h0]
    omega

/-! ## A.6  Local feasibility -/

/-- **`AnchoredFeasible p C P N`.**  Some anchor-allowed subset has positive `p`-adic
valuation of its reciprocal sum, the zero value being treated separately and explicitly. -/
def AnchoredFeasible (p : ℕ) (C P N : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ E ∈ allowed C P N, recipSum E = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum E)

/-- Reformulation of local feasibility purely in terms of numerators. -/
theorem anchoredFeasible_iff_num (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C P N : Finset ℕ) :
    AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔
      ∃ E ∈ allowed C P N, recipSum E = 0 ∨ (p : ℤ) ∣ (recipSum E).num := by
  unfold AnchoredFeasible
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    refine ⟨E, hE, ?_⟩
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact Or.inl h
    · by_cases h0 : recipSum E = 0
      · exact Or.inl h0
      · exact Or.inr ((one_le_padicValRat_iff_dvd_num p h0).1 h)
  · rintro ⟨E, hE, h⟩
    refine ⟨E, hE, ?_⟩
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact Or.inl h
    · by_cases h0 : recipSum E = 0
      · exact Or.inl h0
      · exact Or.inr ((one_le_padicValRat_iff_dvd_num p h0).2 h)

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=10453 sha256=2acacdf4e4127ab7d03a4af848b8e1e1f09afd9ae6579c3a2e64458fcf3b2885 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/Reconciliation.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.BicyclicInterface
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.RouteBridge
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.Reconciliation

/-!
# Anchored route — ledger, reconciliation and integrity

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Three programmes are now tracked, and they are **not merged**:

* **Route S** — the Source / FivePrime / Directed-Selberg / physical-`k = 1` programme
  (`Erdos287.Effectivity.latestEvidence`, cut `Erdos287.Effectivity.latestCutSet`);
* **Route D** — the Direct Reciprocal programme (`Erdos287.Direct.directEvidence`, cut
  `Erdos287.Direct.directCutSet`);
* **Route A** — the anchored / contact-graph *proof-side* programme of this namespace, with
  its own ledger `anchoredEvidence` and cut `anchoredCutSet`.

This file proves that the Route-S and Route-D ledgers, cut sets and the certified finite
frontier are unchanged, that no route discharges another, and that the anchored route adds
**no** finite exclusion and **no** claim about Erdős #287, which remains `OPEN`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-! ## A.25  The anchored ledger -/

/-- Evidence taxonomy of the anchored route. -/
inductive EvidenceAnchored
  /-- reconstructed in the Lean kernel here, with no unproved hypothesis -/
  | kernelProved
  /-- kernel-proved from explicitly named interface hypotheses -/
  | kernelConditional
  /-- open -/
  | openNode
  /-- refuted here -/
  | refuted
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Only kernel-proved content counts as closed. -/
def EvidenceAnchored.isClosed : EvidenceAnchored → Bool
  | .kernelProved => true
  | _ => false

/-- The nodes of the anchored route. -/
inductive AnchoredNode
  /-- exact finite anchored reciprocal state and the reduced-numerator criterion -/
  | reciprocalState
  /-- the finite fingerprint criterion -/
  | fingerprint
  /-- the full prime-power layer equivalence -/
  | primePowerLayer
  /-- the local contact relation and its exact decision -/
  | contactRelation
  /-- exact leaf elimination / forest components -/
  | forestElimination
  /-- exact elimination of isolated cycle components -/
  | cycleElimination
  /-- excess bookkeeping and reduction to a leafless kernel -/
  | cycleRank
  /-- the bridge to the elementary top-layer package -/
  | topLayerBridge
  /-- global rejection of all branching kernels -/
  | branchingKernelRejection
  /-- the unconditional form of that rejection -/
  | unconditionalRejection
  /-- unrestricted Erdős #287 -/
  | erdos287
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Evidence class of each anchored node. -/
def anchoredEvidence : AnchoredNode → EvidenceAnchored
  | .reciprocalState => .kernelProved
  | .fingerprint => .kernelProved
  | .primePowerLayer => .kernelProved
  | .contactRelation => .kernelProved
  | .forestElimination => .kernelProved
  | .cycleElimination => .kernelProved
  | .cycleRank => .kernelProved
  | .topLayerBridge => .kernelProved
  | .branchingKernelRejection => .openNode
  | .unconditionalRejection => .refuted
  | .erdos287 => .openNode

/-- The anchored cut: the single open global step, plus #287 itself. -/
def anchoredCutSet : List AnchoredNode := [.branchingKernelRejection, .erdos287]

/-- **`anchoredCut_all_open`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping. -/
theorem anchoredCut_all_open :
    ∀ n ∈ anchoredCutSet, anchoredEvidence n = EvidenceAnchored.openNode := by
  intro n hn
  fin_cases hn <;> rfl

/-- **`anchored_erdos287_open`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here. -/
theorem anchored_erdos287_open : anchoredEvidence .erdos287 = EvidenceAnchored.openNode := rfl

/-! ## A.26  What the closed anchored nodes actually are -/

/-- **`reciprocalState_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact reduced-numerator criterion,
for every prime. -/
theorem reciprocalState_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .reciprocalState = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (_ : Fact p.Prime) (v : ℚ), v ≠ 0 →
        (1 ≤ padicValRat p v ↔ (p : ℤ) ∣ v.num)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun p hp v hv => @one_le_padicValRat_iff_dvd_num p hp v hv⟩

/-- **`fingerprint_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact fingerprint criterion. -/
theorem fingerprint_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .fingerprint = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (_ : Fact p.Prime) (C P N : Finset ℕ),
        AnchoredFeasible p C P N ↔
          ((0 : ℚ) ∈ valueSet C P N ∨ (p : ℤ) ∣ fingerprint C P N)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun p hp C P N => @anchoredFeasible_iff_fingerprint p hp C P N⟩

/-- **`primePowerLayer_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The full prime-power layer equivalence,
with cofactors divisible by `p` retained. -/
theorem primePowerLayer_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .primePowerLayer = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (_ : Fact p.Prime) (C E : Finset ℕ), E ⊆ C → (∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) → E.Nonempty →
        (p ^ (padicValNat p (lcmOf C) + 1) ∣ cofactorNum C E ↔
          1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum E))) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun p hp _ _ hEC hC hne => @layer_primePower_iff p hp _ _ hEC hC hne⟩

/-- **`contactRelation_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Exact decision of a finite contact
instance. -/
theorem contactRelation_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .contactRelation = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ I : ContactCSP, I.WellFormed → (I.Sat ↔ I.satB = true)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun I hwf => I.sat_iff_satB hwf⟩

/-- **`forestElimination_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Exact leaf elimination and the forest
decision. -/
theorem forestElimination_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .forestElimination = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (I J : ContactCSP), ContactCSP.Peel I J → J.Edges = ∅ →
        (I.Sat ↔ ∀ v ∈ J.V, ∃ b : Bool, J.dom v b = true)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ h hJ => ContactCSP.forest_decision h hJ⟩

/-- **`cycleElimination_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Exact decision of an isolated cycle
component. -/
theorem cycleElimination_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .cycleElimination = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (dom : ℕ → Bool → Bool) (rel : ℕ → ℕ → Bool → Bool → Bool) (x : ℕ) (l : List ℕ),
        (x :: l).Nodup →
          ((cycleCSP dom rel x l).Sat ↔ ∃ a b : Bool,
            transfer dom rel x l a b = true ∧ rel (lastOf x l) x b a = true)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun dom rel x l hnd => cycleCSP_sat_iff dom rel x l hnd⟩

/-- **`cycleRank_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Excess bookkeeping and the reduction of every
finite instance to a leafless branching kernel. -/
theorem cycleRank_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .cycleRank = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ I : ContactCSP, ∃ J, ContactCSP.Peel I J ∧ ContactCSP.Leafless J ∧
        (I.Sat ↔ J.Sat) ∧ J.excess = I.excess) := by
  refine ⟨rfl, fun I => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨J, hJ, hJl⟩ := ContactCSP.exists_peel_to_leafless I
  exact ⟨J, hJ, hJl, hJ.sat_iff, hJ.excess_eq⟩

/-- **`topLayerBridge_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The bridge to the elementary top-layer
package. -/
theorem topLayerBridge_closed :
    anchoredEvidence .topLayerBridge = EvidenceAnchored.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (A : Finset ℕ) (p : ℕ), p.Prime → (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) →
        (∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1) → 1 ≤ topExp A p →
        AnchoredFeasible p (topCofactors A p) (topCofactors A p) ∅) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ hp hpos hsum he => topLayer_anchoredFeasible hp hpos hsum he⟩

/-- **`unconditionalRejection_refuted`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The unconditional global
rejection of branching kernels is false. -/
theorem unconditionalRejection_refuted :
    anchoredEvidence .unconditionalRejection = EvidenceAnchored.refuted ∧
      ¬ BranchingKernelRejection (fun _ => True) :=
  ⟨rfl, branchingKernelRejection_unconditional_false⟩

/-! ## A.27  Reconciliation with the existing routes -/

/-- **`routeS_and_routeD_preserved`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The Route-S and Route-D ledgers and
cut sets are unchanged by this namespace. -/
theorem routeS_and_routeD_preserved :
    Effectivity.latestEvidence .erdos287 = Effectivity.EvidenceLatest.openNode ∧
    Effectivity.latestEvidence .finiteCeilingHere = Effectivity.EvidenceLatest.kernelProved ∧
    Effectivity.latestEvidence .finiteCeilingU2 =
      Effectivity.EvidenceLatest.pendingExternalImport ∧
    Direct.directEvidence .erdos287 = Direct.EvidenceDirect.openNode ∧
    Direct.directEvidence .exactSignedAbsorber = Direct.EvidenceDirect.openNode ∧
    (∀ n ∈ Direct.directCutSet, Direct.directEvidence n = Direct.EvidenceDirect.openNode) :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, Direct.directCut_all_open⟩

/-- **`routes_independent`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  No route discharges another: the cut nodes of
all three routes are simultaneously open. -/
theorem routes_independent :
    (∀ n ∈ Direct.directCutSet, Direct.directEvidence n = Direct.EvidenceDirect.openNode) ∧
    (∀ n ∈ anchoredCutSet, anchoredEvidence n = EvidenceAnchored.openNode) ∧
    Effectivity.latestEvidence .erdos287 = Effectivity.EvidenceLatest.openNode :=
  ⟨Direct.directCut_all_open, anchoredCut_all_open, rfl⟩

/-- **`anchored_finite_frontier_unchanged`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The certified finite frontier
is exactly the existing ceiling `67108856338751594`, with `U2` still pending; the anchored
route adds no finite exclusion. -/
theorem anchored_finite_frontier_unchanged :
    (∀ {A : Finset ℕ} (h : Erdos287Counterexample A),
        A.max' h.nonempty ≤ extendedCeiling → False) ∧
      extendedCeiling = 67108856338751594 ∧
      extendedCeiling < Effectivity.U2 ∧
      Effectivity.latestEvidence .finiteCeilingU2 =
        Effectivity.EvidenceLatest.pendingExternalImport :=
  Direct.finite_frontier_integrity

/-- **`anchored_open_frontier`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  No open anchored node is tagged closed,
and the global branching-kernel rejection is not inhabited here: the only statement about it
proved in this namespace is the refutation of its unconditional form. -/
theorem anchored_open_frontier :
    (∀ n ∈ anchoredCutSet, (anchoredEvidence n).isClosed = false) ∧
      anchoredEvidence .branchingKernelRejection = EvidenceAnchored.openNode ∧
      ¬ BranchingKernelRejection (fun _ => True) := by
  refine ⟨?_, rfl, branchingKernelRejection_unconditional_false⟩
  intro n hn
  fin_cases hn <;> rfl

end Anchored
end Erdos287

@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8010 sha256=edec22d9990a7d2a6b562ad179c9eb799c54e96f187037877e1aead406e3c591 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Anchored/RouteBridge.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Anchored.PrimePowerLayer
import RequestProject.Erdos287.TopLayer
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ProblemStatement

/-!
# Bridges between the anchored route and the existing #287 objects

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Two *proved* bridges are provided — nothing else is imported from, or exported to, the other
routes:

* `padicValRat_recipSum_iff_zmod_inv_sum`: for cofactors prime to `p`, the anchored valuation
  condition `v_p(∑ 1/c) ≥ 1` is **exactly** the mod-`p` inverse-sum condition used in the
  elementary top-layer package;
* `topLayer_anchoredFeasible`: consequently, for any finite set of positive integers with
  reciprocal sum `1` and top `p`-adic exponent `≥ 1`, the cofactor set of the top layer is
  anchored-feasible.  This is the anchored-route reading of the banked theorem
  `Erdos287.topLayer_congruence`.

A third, purely bookkeeping bridge records that the exact #287 counterexample predicate
produces the ambient compiler identity `cofactorNum A A = lcmOf A`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Anchored

/-- If no element of `C` is divisible by the prime `p`, then neither is `lcmOf C`. -/
theorem not_dvd_lcmOf {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) {C : Finset ℕ} (h : ∀ c ∈ C, ¬ p ∣ c) :
    ¬ p ∣ lcmOf C := by
  classical
  have hcop : Nat.Coprime p (lcmOf C) := by
    induction C using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => simp [lcmOf]
    | insert a s ha ih =>
        have h1 : Nat.Coprime p a := (Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd hp).2 (h a (by simp))
        have h2 : Nat.Coprime p (lcmOf s) := ih (fun c hc => h c (by simp [hc]))
        have hins : lcmOf (insert a s) = Nat.lcm a (lcmOf s) := by
          simp [lcmOf, Finset.lcm_insert, lcm]
        rw [hins]
        exact Nat.Coprime.coprime_dvd_right (Nat.lcm_dvd_mul a (lcmOf s))
          (Nat.Coprime.mul_right h1 h2)
  exact (Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd hp).1 hcop

/-- The integral numerator is divisible by `p` exactly when the mod-`p` inverse sum vanishes
(for cofactors prime to `p`). -/
theorem dvd_cofactorNum_iff_zmod_inv_sum (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {C : Finset ℕ}
    (hpos : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) (hnd : ∀ c ∈ C, ¬ p ∣ c) :
    p ∣ cofactorNum C C ↔ (∑ c ∈ C, ((c : ZMod p))⁻¹) = 0 := by
  classical
  haveI : NeZero p := ⟨hp.out.ne_zero⟩
  have hL : ¬ p ∣ lcmOf C := not_dvd_lcmOf hp.out hnd
  have hLz : ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := fun h => hL ((ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 h)
  have hcast : ((cofactorNum C C : ℕ) : ZMod p)
      = ((lcmOf C : ℕ) : ZMod p) * ∑ c ∈ C, ((c : ZMod p))⁻¹ := by
    rw [cofactorNum]
    push_cast
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro c hc
    have hcz : ((c : ℕ) : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := fun h => hnd c hc ((ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 h)
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Finset.dvd_lcm (f := id) hc
    have hk' : lcmOf C = c * k := hk
    have hck : lcmOf C / c = k := by
      rw [hk']
      exact Nat.mul_div_cancel_left k (hpos c hc)
    rw [hck, hk']
    push_cast
    field_simp
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h0 : ((cofactorNum C C : ℕ) : ZMod p) = 0 := (ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff _ _).2 h
    rw [hcast] at h0
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 h0 with h' | h'
    · exact absurd h' hLz
    · exact h'
  · intro h
    refine (ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 ?_
    rw [hcast, h, mul_zero]

/-- **`padicValRat_recipSum_iff_zmod_inv_sum`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge.  For a nonempty
finite set of positive cofactors none of which is divisible by `p`, the anchored valuation
condition is exactly the mod-`p` inverse-sum condition of the elementary top-layer package. -/
theorem padicValRat_recipSum_iff_zmod_inv_sum (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {C : Finset ℕ}
    (hne : C.Nonempty) (hpos : ∀ c ∈ C, 0 < c) (hnd : ∀ c ∈ C, ¬ p ∣ c) :
    1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum C) ↔ (∑ c ∈ C, ((c : ZMod p))⁻¹) = 0 := by
  have hL : ¬ p ∣ lcmOf C := not_dvd_lcmOf hp.out hnd
  have ht : padicValNat p (lcmOf C) = 0 := padicValNat.eq_zero_of_not_dvd hL
  have hiff := layer_primePower_iff p (Finset.Subset.refl C) hpos hne
  rw [ht] at hiff
  rw [← hiff, pow_one]
  exact dvd_cofactorNum_iff_zmod_inv_sum p hpos hnd

/-! ## A.23  The top layer as an anchored state -/

/-- The cofactor set of the top `p`-adic layer of `A`. -/
def topCofactors (A : Finset ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (topLayer A p).image (fun a => ordCompl[p] a)

/-- **`topLayer_anchoredFeasible`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge.  For a finite set `A` of
positive integers with `∑ 1/a = 1` and top `p`-adic exponent at least `1`, the cofactor set of
the top layer is anchored-feasible (with every cofactor mandatorily selected). -/
theorem topLayer_anchoredFeasible {A : Finset ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hpos : ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) (hsum : ∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1) (he : 1 ≤ topExp A p) :
    AnchoredFeasible p (topCofactors A p) (topCofactors A p) ∅ := by
  classical
  haveI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
  -- the top layer is nonempty
  have hAne : A.Nonempty := by
    rcases Finset.eq_empty_or_nonempty A with rfl | h
    · simp [topExp] at he
    · exact h
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀A, ha₀⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup A hAne (fun a => Nat.factorization a p)
  have ha₀top : a₀ ∈ topLayer A p := mem_topLayer.2 ⟨ha₀A, ha₀.symm⟩
  have hTne : (topLayer A p).Nonempty := ⟨a₀, ha₀top⟩
  have hCne : (topCofactors A p).Nonempty := hTne.image _
  -- the cofactors are positive and prime to `p`
  have hCpos : ∀ c ∈ topCofactors A p, 0 < c := by
    intro c hc
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hc
    have haA : a ∈ A := (mem_topLayer.1 ha).1
    exact Nat.ordCompl_pos p (hpos a haA).ne'
  have hCnd : ∀ c ∈ topCofactors A p, ¬ p ∣ c := by
    intro c hc
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hc
    have haA : a ∈ A := (mem_topLayer.1 ha).1
    exact Nat.not_dvd_ordCompl hp (hpos a haA).ne'
  -- the mod-`p` inverse sum over the cofactors is the banked top-layer congruence
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun a => ordCompl[p] a) (topLayer A p) := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    have hea : Nat.factorization a p = topExp A p := (mem_topLayer.1 ha).2
    have heb : Nat.factorization b p = topExp A p := (mem_topLayer.1 hb).2
    have ra : p ^ (Nat.factorization a p) * ordCompl[p] a = a :=
      Nat.ordProj_mul_ordCompl_eq_self a p
    have rb : p ^ (Nat.factorization b p) * ordCompl[p] b = b :=
      Nat.ordProj_mul_ordCompl_eq_self b p
    have hab' : a / p ^ topExp A p = b / p ^ topExp A p := by
      have hc : ordCompl[p] a = ordCompl[p] b := hab
      rwa [hea, heb] at hc
    rw [← ra, ← rb, hea, heb, hab']
  have hsum0 : (∑ c ∈ topCofactors A p, ((c : ZMod p))⁻¹) = 0 := by
    rw [topCofactors, Finset.sum_image (fun a ha b hb h => hinj ha hb h)]
    exact topLayer_congruence A p hp hpos hsum he
  have hval : 1 ≤ padicValRat p (recipSum (topCofactors A p)) :=
    (padicValRat_recipSum_iff_zmod_inv_sum p hCne hCpos hCnd).2 hsum0
  exact ⟨topCofactors A p, mem_allowed.2 ⟨Finset.Subset.refl _, Finset.Subset.refl _, by simp⟩,
    Or.inr hval⟩

/-! ## A.24  The exact counterexample predicate -/

/-- **`counterexample_cofactorNum_eq_lcmOf`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For an exact #287
counterexample the ambient compiler identity holds in the anchored conventions. -/
theorem counterexample_cofactorNum_eq_lcmOf {A : Finset ℕ} (h : Erdos287Counterexample A) :
    cofactorNum A A = lcmOf A := by
  have hpos : ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a := fun a ha => lt_trans Nat.zero_lt_one (h.one_lt a ha)
  have hrec : recipSum A = ((cofactorNum A A : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((lcmOf A : ℕ) : ℚ) :=
    recipSum_eq_cofactorNum_div (Finset.Subset.refl A) hpos
  have h1 : recipSum A = 1 := h.sum_one
  have hLq : ((lcmOf A : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (lcmOf_pos hpos).ne'
  rw [h1, eq_comm, div_eq_one_iff_eq hLq] at hrec
  exact_mod_cast hrec

end Anchored
end Erdos287
